questions.prompt: What can a split vote cause in a Raft cluster?
options: Two leaders in the same term
A follower voting twice in one term
A term that ends with no leader, delaying progress
questions.explanation: Split votes only hurt liveness: the term ends leaderless and a new election must run. Two leaders in one term is impossible because each server still votes once per term and majorities overlap.

questions.prompt: An operator sets heartbeat interval to 100 ms and election timeout to a random value in 110 to 130 ms. What is the most likely symptom?
options: Frequent unnecessary elections, because one delayed heartbeat lets a follower time out
Log entries being committed out of order
Followers refusing to vote for anyone
questions.explanation: The election timeout should be several heartbeat intervals long so a single lost or slow heartbeat does not trigger an election. Here a follower gets roughly one heartbeat per timeout, so any jitter causes leader churn. Safety is unaffected, so out-of-order commits cannot happen.

questions.prompt: Why should a server pick a fresh random timeout every time it resets its election timer, rather than choosing one value at startup?
options: Because the term number is used as the random seed
So that two servers that happened to tie once are unlikely to tie again on the retry
Because the leader assigns each follower's timeout in its heartbeat
To make sure the timeout increases exponentially after each failure
questions.explanation: If two servers drew nearly equal fixed timeouts, they would collide in every election. Re-randomizing on each reset breaks the tie with high probability on the next round. Raft does not use exponential backoff for elections, and leaders do not assign timeouts.
